display.title: Vayeira: Avraham Avinu, the Man of Kindness
display.summary_short: Why we should know the week's sedra, and how Avraham Avinu's love of chesed in Parshas Vayeira teaches children to do kindness at home and in school.
display.summary_long: A parsha talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, aired on 16 Cheshvan 5750. Uncle Yossi explains that besides the day and the date, we should know which sedra's week it is, because every parsha has a living lesson. In Parshas Vayeira we learn that Avraham Avinu was a man of chesed: he set up a tent by the road with food and drink for travelers, and asked them to thank Hashem with a brachah. On the hot day after his bris, Hashem kept travelers away so he could rest, but missing the chance to do kindness hurt Avraham more than the bris, so Hashem sent three angels dressed as ordinary people. Since the deeds of the fathers are a sign for the children, we follow Avraham by helping our parents, our brothers and sisters, and our classmates, and Avraham, in Gan Eden, blesses children who do so. The talk ends with the happy chapter of Yitzchak's birth when Avraham was a hundred years old, since Torah is the source of true happiness.
display.lesson: We are Avraham's children: look for every chance to do a favor for parents, siblings and classmates.
